The results within this report relate only to the items tested. 2 Abstract An innovative sorbent structure of trapped small amines in hierarchical nanoporous capsules (HNC) embedded in porous electrospun fibers (PEF) was developed for direct air capture (DAC). This involves tailoring both sorbent and PEF materials to achieve a compact system for DAC with high capacity for CO at concentrations typically available in air and at near ambient conditions. 2 The sorbent material was prepared by an interfacial reaction to form a polyamide (PA) coating on amine-loaded mesoporous silica. The optimized sorbent material exhibited CO capacity as high 2 as 4.88 mmol/g under humid DAC conditions and negligible loss (<1%) during 10 cyclic heating- cooling operations. The PA-coated sorbent also showed fast adsorption and desorption kinetics, with <20% t increase compared to uncoated sorbent. After incorporating the optimized sorbent 1/2 material into PEF, the structured sorbent had a CO capacity of approximately 4.0 mmol/g under 2 humid DAC conditions, with capacity loss of 0.17% per cycle and t increase less than 10%. 1/2 A 4-step process was designed to capture CO from air using the optimized sorbent. Aspen 2 Adsorption Simulator was used to fit the experimentally measured breakthrough curves and extract equilibrium and kinetic data. Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) was conducted to calculate the CO capture cost. For a DAC plant with CO productivity of approximately 3,000 tonne/year, the 2 2 levelized cost of CO capture was $612/tonne, with the largest contribution of 44.33% from the 2 fixed operation cost. Increasing CO productivity, while maintaining similar fixed operation cost, 2 is expected to significantly reduce the CO capture cost. A sensitivity study was also conducted 2 to understand the influence of total plant cost, sorbent cost, CO concentration in the feed, sorbent 2 mat lifetime, sorbent regeneration electricity, and adsorption blower pressure drop on the levelized cost of CO capture, revealing a capture cost range of $520-870/tonne. 2 3 Acknowledgments We gratefully acknowledge financial support by the US Department of Energy (Contract Number DE-FE0031969).
